title: Contract-local DDL parity for canonical Durable Authorized Injection State

phases.objective: Add one explicit contract-local MySQL DDL surface for the canonical Durable Authorized Injection State tables and prove exact parity with the existing registry schema contract and SQL access paths without changing runtime ownership.

e2e_journeys.actor: Spec 014 durable authorized injection DDL guard
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Canonical registry schema contract, registry SQL source, and contract-local DDL file
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The DDL declares exactly the canonical state and rollback tables, required columns, digests, uniqueness, foreign key, CAS fields, and no-secrets constraints while remaining outside every promoted migration path.
steps: Read the canonical exported schema contract and exact table names.
Read the registry SQL markers for state load, rollback load, state insert, rollback CAS update, and immutable rollback insert.
Parse the contract-local DDL and require exactly one CREATE TABLE statement for each canonical table.
Verify state identity, Receipt/Readback/bundle digests, active generation, row version, JSON record, and no-secrets columns.
Verify one immutable rollback per injection, unique rollback digest, and foreign-key binding to the state row.
Reject destructive DDL, migration-ledger mutation, Route/Server changes, and any promotion or Apply authority.
assertions: The canonical registry implementation is not modified.
DDL table and column names match the SQL used by the canonical registry.
Rollback remains append-only and state rollback remains row-version CAS guarded.
The DDL is contract-local and not a migration candidate or promoted runtime migration.
No live database, provider, deployment, main, or Production authority is granted.

phases.objective: Create, authorize, dry-run, and apply a separately reviewed migration candidate for these tables only after live absence and compatibility readback.
blockers: The DDL remains contract-local and is not included in the governed runtime migration sequence.
No live table-absence, collation, engine, parent compatibility, or privilege readback exists.
No checksum-bound migration authorization, typed confirmation, dry-run, Apply, or migration-ledger evidence exists.
No signed same-cycle schema verification exists for these two tables.

phases.objective: After a separately governed Apply, prove restart reconstruction and rollback CAS against live same-cycle signed schema readback without introducing a second persistence path.
Observe one separately authorized non-production canary only after the canonical schema is applied and mounted through fixed runtime composition.
This repository-only DDL contract grants no migration Apply, provider, deployment, main, or Production authority.
